content.thinking:
I'm working through the postmortem now. The account page errors line up with a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py from 04:13 to 04:19, and the flag was partially on at 04:13 and fully on from 04:14 onward. I'm tracing how the flag rollout timing matches the error window.

I'm checking the flag provider history and production changes, and finding that none were recorded before the errors, so the flag flip shows up only in the logs. I'm ruling out an earlier change for now, since the replicas all ran one unnamed revision as of that check, and no deploys are on record.

I'm checking whether a deploy could explain the onset: no deploys or production changes are recorded in the day before, and all replicas were running one unnamed revision when I read them. But that only shows nothing was recorded, not that the revision was in place and healthy before 04:13, so I can't rule it out yet.

I'm mapping the causal chain next, starting from the symptom: shoppers' account page requests failing with server errors while the error rate climbs. I'm also setting the ClientDisconnected errors aside as baseline noise that ended at 04:13 and was present before the onset while the service was healthy.

I'm tying the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py to the monthly-spend flag, which started evaluating on at 04:13 and was on for every evaluation from 04:14. Before that it was off for every evaluation, so the flag change lines up with the onset, but no change to it is recorded anywhere.

I'm weighing whether the flag change itself is a contributing factor: it turned on without any recorded change in the flag provider history, so Argus had no record to act on. Had it been recorded, the response could have been shorter. I'll note that as a contributing factor and propose an action item to find out how the flag came to evaluate on with no recorded change.

I'm tracing the root cause through the code: the spend summary divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month, and that path only runs once the flag is on. The division at line 47 fits the ZeroDivisionError, though the error itself doesn't show what the denominator is, so the mechanism still rests on that code reading.

I'm writing up the root cause now: with the monthly-spend flag on, the spend summary divides this month's spend by this month's purchase count without guarding against zero, which fails at spend_summary.py:47 for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month. I'm also phrasing the plain-language version, noting that the record shows the flag evaluating on but not who turned it on.

I'm drafting the forward-looking risk and then the contributing factors. The point to make is that shoppers with no purchases this month could keep hitting the failure while the monthly spend feature stays on, and that the flag could come on again without any change appearing in the provider's history. I'm also starting on the first contributing factor, that the divide-by-zero path reached production with the flag on and no test seemed to exercise a zero-purchase month under that setting.

I'm working out the second contributing factor now: the flag went from partial to fully on within about a minute, and I don't see a staged rollout gate on error rate that would have held it back.

I'm working out the remaining contributing factors now: the flag's change never appeared in the flag provider's history or the change events, so Argus had nothing recorded it could have reversed. I'm drafting a proposed item to find out how the flag came on without a recorded change and to route every change through the recorded provider.

I'm listing the remaining action items now: one to require flag-on tests with empty-input cases before a flag goes live, one to roll out monthly-spend-feature in stages that halt and revert on account page error rate, and one to find out how the flag came on without any recorded change. I'm also noting the item to make every flag change go through the recorded provider.

I'm weighing whether to propose switching monthly-spend-feature off until the fix in PR #557 is merged, since the record doesn't show anyone doing that and the service was still broken.

I'm putting the lessons together now: the investigator's early naming of the flag and the ZeroDivisionError is one thing that went well, and the draft fix in pull request #557 with its regression test is another.

I'm settling on the went-wrong side now: no one turned the flag off while Argus had the incident, because the flag change never showed up in the provider's history or change events, so nothing automatic could act on it and the service stayed broken when Argus stopped.

I'm settling the went-wrong and got-lucky lists: I'll leave went-wrong empty, since the refusal to act was the designed behavior, and got-lucky empty too. Then I'm noting the assumptions: the 04:13 onset comes from the investigator's placement and the logs, and I'm taking the account page failures as the source of the service's error rate even though the series covers all requests.

I'm checking whether anything else was ruled out, like an earlier deploy or a rollout split: the change events show no production changes the day before the onset, and all replicas are on one revision. The flag provider's history doesn't clear the flag itself, since the logs show it was on.

I'm checking whether the flag provider's history shows any change before the onset. It shows none by anyone but Argus in the hour before, so the flag turning on isn't in the record of changes. I also haven't seen whether the revision the replicas ran was in place before 04:13, so a change to it isn't ruled out yet. The ClientDisconnected errors start well before the onset and stop at 04:13, while the account page error rate sits at its usual baseline, so they don't explain the spike.

I'm checking the flag's timeline against the logs: it was off until a point near 04:13, came on for only part of the evaluations there, and was fully on from a later point. None of the production change events or flag provider history records what switched it, so that cause is still unseen, and I can't rule out a change to the single revision the replicas were running.

I'm laying out the symptom, the onset, and the first step of the causal chain, which is the account page failures and their timing against the flag's switch-on.

I'm checking which test cases would have caught the zero-purchase path with the flag on, and I'm weighing how the Investigator and Code-Fix agents each contributed early on.

I'm settling the contributing factors and action items, and I'm checking that the tokens in my draft point to the right rows. Averages and counts I'll describe without naming numbers, and I'm keeping the flag's switch-on and the lack of any recorded change as the open point.

I'm settling on the wording for the remaining steps, keeping the flag's switch-on as the open point and avoiding any figures.

action_items.item: Turn monthly-spend-feature off on io-shop until the fix in PR #557 is merged and deployed.

Before any feature flag on io-shop can be enabled in production, require tests that run the code behind the flag with the flag on, including the case of a shopper with no purchases in the current period.
Roll out flags such as monthly-spend-feature in stages that pause and switch the flag back off automatically when the account page error rate rises.
Find out how monthly-spend-feature came on with no change in the flag provider's history or in the production change events.
Make every change to io-shop feature flags go through the flag provider so that the change appears in its history.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors from the onset, and the account page error rate kept climbing until it was highest at {Gbac1.7}.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, from {G5309.3}; this error did not appear in the log lines before the onset.

ruled_out.what: The client-disconnect failures on account pages: they were logged from well before the onset while the account page error rate stayed at its usual {Gbac1.6}, and they stopped at the onset.

A recorded deploy, release or flag change by anyone but Argus: the production change events for the day before the onset came back empty, and so did the flag provider's history for the hour before it was read.

causal_chain.step: The monthly-spend-feature flag had been off for every evaluation through {G7e5d.4}. It was on for part of the evaluations at {G971b.6} (on {G971b.2}, off {G971b.1} of {G971b.3}) and on for every evaluation from {Gce95.4}. Neither the production change events read at {T9.1} nor the flag provider's history read at {T15.1} shows this change, so the record does not show what switched the flag. All replicas ran the same revision when read at {T10.1}, but the record does not show whether that revision was already running before the onset, so a change to it was not ruled out.

With the flag on, the account page runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month and fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A setting that shows shoppers their spending this month came on, and the code behind it likely fails when a shopper has bought nothing yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages returned errors.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that ran the spend summary with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on for shoppers.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division failure would have been found before the flag reached any shopper, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from on for part of the evaluations to on for all of them by the next minute. No rollout stage was seen that held or reversed it as account page errors rose.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that stopped on the rising account page error rate would have kept the failures to a small share of shoppers and switched the flag back off.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The flag coming on did not appear in the flag provider's history or in the production change events, so the change was not in the record of what changed.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: With the change recorded, Argus could have acted on C1 and turned the flag off, which would have ended the failures sooner instead of leaving it to a person.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No on-call incident was linked to the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person could have turned the flag off once Argus left undoing it to a person, which would have shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed C1, which named the monthly-spend-feature flag and the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 from the log lines.
Argus did not undo a change it could not find in the record of what changed, and left that to a person.
The Code-Fix Agent opened draft pull request #557 with a proposed fix and a regression test for a person to review.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases they made this month without handling a shopper who bought nothing this month, so for any shopper who has bought before but not this month the page raises ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages of shoppers who have not bought anything this month could keep failing while the monthly spend feature stays on, and the feature could come on again without any change showing in the flag provider's history.
